messages:
Maya: Flagged a support convo where a user accidentally deleted a workspace. Our current confirmation modal reads 'Delete workspace' with a single 'Delete' button. Support wants clearer consequences and a stronger safety net. Screenshot in Figma.
Tom: Oof. Definitely need to avoid ambiguous CTAs. Proposals: make primary destructive label explicit: 'Delete workspace and all data' or 'Permanently delete workspace'. Also require typing workspace name to confirm.
Rina: Typing the workspace name is good, but we should provide exact copy guidance. Example helper: 'Type the workspace name to confirm: Acme Corp' and show a readonly example. Also show a small list of what will be deleted: 'models, uploads, logs, settings'.
Alex: Accessibility nits: when modal opens, set focus to the text input. The 'Confirm' button should be disabled until input matches exactly. Screen readers need an aria-describedby with the consequences text. Also ensure the input has aria-label='Confirm workspace name'.
Maya: Draft copy variants:
1) Explicit legal: Title: 'Permanently delete workspace' Body: 'This action cannot be undone. Deleting the workspace will remove all models, uploads, billing history, and settings.' Helper: 'Type the workspace name to confirm: "{workspace_name}"' Primary CTA: 'Permanently delete' Secondary: 'Cancel'
2) Plain language: Title: 'Delete workspace' Body: 'Everything in this workspace will be permanently removed, including models and files.' Helper: 'Type "{workspace_name}" to confirm' Primary CTA: 'Delete workspace' Secondary: 'Never mind'
3) Safer-first: Title: 'Archive or delete workspace' Body: 'If you only need to stop activity, consider archiving instead. Deleting removes all data.' Buttons: Primary 'Archive workspace' Secondary 'Delete workspace' with secondary being destructive (requires name confirmation).
Tom: I prefer variant 1 for enterprise clarity. Avoid 'Never mind' as it sounds informal. Also prefer 'Permanently delete' CTA so users understand finality.
Rina: Microcopy for the disabled state: show 'Type the workspace name to enable deletion' in a subtle tone. Once they'd typed, swap to a live region update: 'Workspace name matches. Delete button enabled.' That helps SR users.
Alex: Keyboard affordances: input should accept paste, but warn if trailing spaces. If mismatch on case-sensitivity, decide if confirmation should be case-insensitive. I'd vote case-sensitive to avoid accidental matches, but show note 'case-sensitive'.
Maya: Legal says avoid words like 'forever' and prefers 'permanently' or 'irreversible'. Also they want a link to the retention policy in the modal body.
Tom: Tooltip for the 'Delete' button on hover: 'This will permanently remove the workspace and its data. Audit logs will record the action.' Keep tooltip copy <120 chars.
Rina: Localization: keep strings short (title < 40 chars where possible) and avoid colloquialisms. Provide placeholders for workspace_name and count numbers.
Alex: Implementation checklist: role='alertdialog', aria-labelledby points to title, aria-describedby points to body+list, focus to input on open, ensure keyboard-only users can enable/activate via enter once match occurs. Live region for state changes. Log audit event WORKSPACE_DELETE_INIT & WORKSPACE_DELETE_COMPLETE with user ID and workspace id.
Maya: Final decision: go with variant 1 (enterprise/legal-friendly) + required name confirmation, case-sensitive, show deleted-items list, include retention-policy link, disabled primary until exact match, aria-live feedback, and 'Permanently delete' CTA. Change secondary to 'Cancel'. Tooltip text as above.
